author: Sister Maren, wandering astronomer
pages:
#The Stones of the Sky

Across the north stand carved monoliths, each marked with a constellation that glows faintly at night. There are thirteen of them, one for each of the signs that rule the heavens. Touch a stone and you receive the blessing of its sign.

But mark this: the sky allows only one blessing at a time. Touching a new stone replaces the old one.

#The Guardian Stones

Three stones stand together in a triangle, as they always have: the Warrior, the Mage and the Thief. They are the guardians of the other ten.

The Warrior hastens learning in the arts of combat and the forge. The Mage hastens learning in all the schools of magic and enchantment. The Thief hastens learning in the quiet arts: light armour, sneaking, locks, pockets, persuasion and alchemy.

#The Lady, the Lord and the Lover

The Lady's blessing makes wounds close and breath return more quickly.

The Lord hardens the skin like armour and turns aside some of the force of hostile magic.

The Lover favours no single art but quickens learning in all of them, a little.

#The Atronach and the Apprentice

These two are opposites, and wise mages choose between them with care.

The Atronach deepens the well of magicka and drinks in part of any spell cast against you, but the well refills slowly.

The Apprentice makes magicka flow back swiftly, but leaves you more vulnerable to hostile magic.

#The Ritual, the Serpent and the Shadow

These three grant powers that may be called upon once each day, with the old words or simply by will.

The Ritual raises the restless dead from the earth to fight at your side for a short while.

The Serpent strikes a chosen foe with paralysing venom.

The Shadow lets you vanish from sight for the span of a minute.

#The Steed and the Tower

The Steed lets you carry far more, and your armour weighs on you no longer, so that you move a little more swiftly.

The Tower, once each day, will open a lock for you as if by its own wish.

#How to Find Them

The stones stand in quiet places, often on round platforms of old stone, ringed by mossy pillars. At night their sigils glow, and sparks of light rise from them toward their stars. Look for that light from the hilltops.
